mainTopic: How the תנאים learn rulings from פסוקים (causing a מום, guarding doubtful תרומה), שמואל's ruling like רבי שמעון on letting blood from a בכור, and a new משנה on slitting a בכור's ear.
overview: This amud first finishes a ברייתא: you may not even cause a מום indirectly, for example by putting food on a בכור's ear so a dog bites it. The גמרא then says that the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about guarding doubtful תרומה also comes from a פסוק, 'משמרת תרומתי', read as plural or as singular. It asks whether this means רבי אליעזר holds יש אם למקרא, and contradicts that from a ברייתא about a Hebrew maidservant, where רבי אליעזר follows the spelling. The answer is that the תרומה dispute is really about whether doubtful תרומה counts as 'fit for you', since אליהו may one day declare it pure. Next, שמואל rules like רבי שמעון. The גמרא proves he must mean רבי שמעון of the ברייתא, because he has already ruled elsewhere that דבר שאין מתכוין is permitted. A new משנה then teaches that someone who slits a בכור's ear may never slaughter it according to רבי אליעזר, while the חכמים allow it once another blemish appears. The גמרא begins to challenge whether רבי אליעזר really makes a penalty last forever, and that challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Even causing a blemish indirectly is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: the words 'כל מום' teach that you may not even arrange for a dog to bite the animal's ear and make a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: [I would know] only that a person may not put a blemish on the animal himself. How do we know he may not put pressed figs or dough on its ear so a dog will come and eat it (and bite the ear)? The verse says 'any blemish': both a blemish you make yourself and 'any' blemish, even an indirect one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא it began earlier. The ברייתא learns from the extra word 'כל' that even an indirect מום is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the word 'כל', we would only know that you may not cut the animal yourself. The extra word 'כל' widens the rule to cover a trick where a dog does the damage for you. This ברייתא shows the תנאים building rulings from small words in a פסוק, and the גמרא will now say the same is true of the next dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemish that disqualifies an animal
The verse teaches (introduces the source in a פסוק)

phrases.english: [I would know] only that one may not put a blemish on it;
from where do we know that one may not bring pressed figs or dough
and place it on the ear
so that a dog will come and eat it?
The verse says: 'any blemish'
both a blemish and 'any' blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that the גמרא was quoting before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra word 'כל' in 'כל מום' forbids even an indirect blemish, such as setting things up so a dog bites the animal's ear.

steps.title: This dispute also comes from a verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the dispute about guarding תרומה is also about how to read a פסוק, and quotes 'משמרת תרומתי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too they disagree about how to read verses. As רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, and ריש לקיש said the same, and רב נחמן said the same in the name of רבה בר אבוה: 'And I, behold, I have given you the safekeeping of My תרומות.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the dispute of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about guarding תרומה and says it is also rooted in a פסוק. This step sets up the verse; the next step explains how each side reads it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three chains of אמוראים all agree on the source: the phrase 'משמרת תרומתי', the safekeeping of My תרומות. The key word is תרומתי, which looks like it could be plural. How each תנא reads that one word will explain his opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree about how to read verses

phrases.english: Here too they disagree about verses,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about guarding תרומה.

phrases.english: as Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel,
and so said Reish Lakish,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: and so said Rav Nachman in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
'And I, behold, I have given you
the safekeeping of My terumot.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Just as the ברייתא in step 1 built rulings from a verse, the גמרא now shows that this dispute is also about a verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute about guarding תרומה depends on how to read 'משמרת תרומתי'.

steps.title: Plural or singular: each side's reading
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר reads תרומתי as plural, so even doubtful תרומה must be guarded. רבי יהושע reads it as singular, so only certainly pure תרומה must be guarded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר holds: the verse is talking about two kinds of תרומה, one that is pure and one whose purity is in doubt, and the Merciful One said: guard it. And רבי יהושע says: it is written 'My teruma' (singular).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the word תרומתי leads each תנא to his opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר goes by how the word is pronounced, as a plural, so it covers two kinds: תרומה טהורה and תרומה תלויה. Both need guarding. רבי יהושע goes by the spelling, which has no ו and can be read as singular, so only one kind (the pure kind) must be guarded.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Hanging' תרומה, whose purity is in doubt
The Merciful One (ה׳, as the Giver of the Torah)
It is written (how the word is spelled)

steps.whatToRemember: Pronounced as plural, תרומתי means two kinds of תרומה must be guarded (רבי אליעזר). Spelled as singular, it means only pure תרומה must be guarded (רבי יהושע).

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds:
the verse speaks of two kinds of teruma,
one, teruma that is pure,
and one, teruma that is 'hanging' (in doubt),
and the Merciful One said: make a guarding for it.
And Rabbi Yehoshua: 'My teruma' is written.
phrases.notes: The word is spelled without a ו, so it can be read as singular.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: בִּשְׁתֵּי תְּרוּמוֹת הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how each תנא reads the verse quoted in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר reads the verse as plural, so doubtful תרומה must also be guarded. רבי יהושע reads it as singular, so only pure תרומה must be guarded.

steps.title: Does רבי אליעזר follow the pronunciation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws out of step 3 that רבי אליעזר seems to hold יש אם למקרא, that the pronunciation decides the meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that רבי אליעזר holds that the way a word is read (pronounced) is what counts?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out what רבי אליעזר's reading seems to mean: that he follows how a word is pronounced. This sets up a challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר read תרומתי as plural even though the spelling allows a singular reading. That fits the rule יש אם למקרא, meaning the pronunciation is the 'mother' (the authority). The question prepares a contradiction from another source.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (draws out what a view implies)
The pronunciation of the verse is the authority

steps.confusionAlert: יש אם למקרא means we follow how the word is pronounced. Its opposite is that we follow how the word is spelled. Don't mix them up: רבי אליעזר followed the pronunciation (plural), and רבי יהושע followed the spelling (singular).

phrases.english: Is that to say that Rabbi Eliezer holds
that the reading is the 'mother' (the authority)?
phrases.notes: In other words, the way the word is pronounced, not how it's spelled, decides its meaning.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר יֵשׁ אֵם לַמִּקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule out of רבי אליעזר's reading in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אליעזר really holds יש אם למקרא in general.

steps.title: A contradiction from the Hebrew maidservant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a contradiction with a ברייתא about 'בבגדו בה', starting with רבי עקיבא's view that once the master spread his cloak over her, she may not be sold again.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they raised a contradiction: 'In his betraying her' (בבגדו בה): once he spread his cloak over her, she may no longer be sold. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא to contradict the idea that רבי אליעזר follows the pronunciation. This step quotes רבי עקיבא's part, and the next step brings רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא connects the word בבגדו to בגד, a garment: spreading his cloak over her means taking her as a wife. After that she can no longer be sold. רבי עקיבא's reading is the one that follows the pronunciation, which sets up a clash with what step 4 said about רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: In his betraying, which sounds like בגד, a garment

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
'In his betraying her':
phrases.notes: שמות 21:8. The word sounds like בגד, a garment.

phrases.english: once he spread his cloak over her,
one is no longer permitted to sell her,
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to test the idea from step 4 that רבי אליעזר holds יש אם למקרא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea from step 4 that רבי אליעזר holds יש אם למקרא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In this ברייתא, the reading that follows the pronunciation of 'בבגדו' belongs to רבי עקיבא. That suggests רבי אליעזר may hold the opposite principle, which would clash with how he read תרומתי. Step 6 completes the contradiction.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר follows the spelling in the cloak case
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי אליעזר says that once the father dealt deceitfully with her, he may not sell her again. This contradicts the idea from step 4 that he follows the pronunciation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: since he dealt deceitfully with her, he may not sell her again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the contradiction it started in step 5. It shows that רבי אליעזר learns from the way the word is written, not the way it is read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בבגדו is written without a יו״ד, so it can be read as 'his betraying' (בָּגְדוֹ). רבי אליעזר learns from this spelling, which is the view of יש אם למסורת. In step 4, though, his view on תרומה seemed to be יש אם למקרא, so the גמרא has caught him holding two opposite rules.

keyTerms.meaning: the written spelling decides the meaning

steps.confusionAlert: Here רבי עקיבא is the one who follows the pronunciation ('his cloak'), and רבי אליעזר follows the spelling ('his betrayal'). That is the opposite of what step 4 said about רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
since he dealt deceitfully with her,
phrases.notes: He reads the word בבגדו the way it is spelled, without a יו״ד, so it means 'his betraying,' not 'his cloak.'

phrases.english: he is no longer allowed to sell her!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: כֵּיוָן שֶׁבָּגַד בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contradiction begun in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim from step 4 that רבי אליעזר holds יש אם למקרא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the cloak case רבי אליעזר learns from the spelling, so he holds יש אם למסורת. That clashes with reading תרומתי by its pronunciation.

steps.title: The dispute is really about what counts as fit for you
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the תרומה dispute is not about spelling or pronunciation. It is about whether תרומה of doubtful purity counts as 'fit for you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here they disagree about this. רבי יהושע holds: guard what is fit for you, and do not guard what is not fit for you. רבי אליעזר holds: this doubtful תרומה is also fit, because perhaps אליהו will come and declare it pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by giving a new explanation of the תרומה dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides learn from the word 'לך' (for you) in the פסוק. רבי יהושע says only definitely pure תרומה is fit to eat, so only that must be guarded. רבי אליעזר says doubtful תרומה may one day be declared pure by אליהו, so it also counts as fit. Now nothing ties רבי אליעזר to יש אם למקרא.

keyTerms.meaning: אליהו הנביא, who will settle doubtful cases in the future
and he will declare it pure

steps.whatToRemember: The תרומה dispute is about whether doubtful תרומה is 'fit for you.' It is not about how to read a word.

phrases.english: Rather, here they disagree about this:
Rabbi Yehoshua holds:
what is fit for you, guard,
phrases.notes: The word 'for you' comes from the פסוק 'נתתי לך את משמרת תרומתי' (במדבר 18:8).

phrases.english: and what is not fit for you, do not guard,
and Rabbi Eliezer holds:
this one is also fit,
since perhaps Eliyahu will come and declare it pure.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the basis of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute depended on reading תרומתי as plural or singular, which would make רבי אליעזר hold יש אם למקרא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is about whether doubtful תרומה counts as 'fit for you,' so it has nothing to do with יש אם למקרא.

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to letting blood from a בכור. רב יהודה reports that שמואל ruled like רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the halacha follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ruling of שמואל that follows רבי שמעון. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling does not say which statement of רבי שמעון it means. The next step depends on that missing detail.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section, going back to the משנה about letting blood from a בכור

steps.title: Which רבי שמעון did שמואל mean?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks which רבי שמעון שמואל meant. It cannot be רבי שמעון of our משנה, because שמואל already ruled that an unintended act is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenged this: Which רבי שמעון? If you say the רבי שמעון of our משנה, hasn't שמואל already taught us that an unintended act is permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenges the ruling. If it refers to our משנה, שמואל would be saying something he has already said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי שמעון allows letting blood from a בכור even though a מום may result, because the מום is not intended. That is just the rule of דבר שאין מתכוין. שמואל has already ruled that דבר שאין מתכוין is permitted, so ruling it again would teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: an act whose forbidden result is not intended

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak challenged it:
Which Rabbi Shimon?
If you say the Rabbi Shimon of our משנה,
phrases.notes: In our משנה, רבי שמעון allows letting the blood even though a מום may result.

phrases.english: hasn't Shmuel already taught us before this
that an unintended act is permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: הֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of שמואל in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that שמואל's ruling refers to רבי שמעון of our משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it did, שמואל would be repeating his own ruling that דבר שאין מתכוין is permitted, and an אמורא does not repeat himself for no reason.

steps.title: Proof that שמואל already ruled on unintended acts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes two reports showing that רב ruled like רבי יהודה and שמואל ruled like רבי שמעון on דבר שאין מתכוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. And רב חנין בר אשי said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון. And רב חייא בר אבין teaches it without the people who passed it on: רב said the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, and שמואל said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the challenge from step 9. It shows that שמואל's ruling on unintended acts is already well known.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה forbids דבר שאין מתכוין, and רבי שמעון permits it. Two separate reports already have שמואל ruling like רבי שמעון on this question. So his statement in step 8 must be about a different opinion of רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: but surely (brings a source as proof)
without naming the people who passed it on

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל is already known to rule like רבי שמעון that דבר שאין מתכוין is permitted, so his ruling in step 8 must mean something else.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But surely Rav Chiya bar Ashi said in the name of Rav:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה is the one who forbids an unintended act.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חָנִין בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: and Rav Chanin bar Ashi said in the name of Shmuel:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין מַתְנֵי בְּלָא גַּבְרֵי —
phrases.english: and Rav Chiya bar Avin teaches it without the people who passed it on:
Rav said: The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda,
and Shmuel said: The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the evidence behind the challenge in step 9
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל has already ruled that דבר שאין מתכוין is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two reports, from רב חנין בר אשי and from רב חייא בר אבין, of שמואל ruling like רבי שמעון against רב, who rules like רבי יהודה

steps.title: שמואל meant רבי שמעון of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל was ruling like רבי שמעון of the ברייתא, not רבי שמעון of our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, שמואל meant רבי שמעון of the ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9. שמואל was ruling like רבי שמעון of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 asked why שמואל would need to rule like רבי שמעון of our משנה, since he already ruled that an unintended act is permitted. The answer is that he meant a different statement of רבי שמעון, from the ברייתא. That ruling adds something new: one may let blood even if it causes a blemish, and may even slaughter the animal because of that blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי שמעון as quoted in the ברייתא, not in our משנה

phrases.english: Rather, it is Rabbi Shimon of the baraita.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא quoted earlier, on 33b, about letting blood from a בכור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 9, after step 10 showed that שמואל had already ruled like רבי שמעון on דבר שאין מתכוין.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a different source: the same name, but a different statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל was ruling like רבי שמעון of our משנה, which would repeat what he already said.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל was ruling like רבי שמעון of the ברייתא, which adds a new point.

steps.title: A version where שמואל says it openly
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי quotes שמואל's ruling with the words 'of the ברייתא' stated openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא son of רב אידי taught it clearly: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, the halacha follows רבי שמעון of the ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer. In רב שישא's version, שמואל's ruling openly says 'רבי שמעון of the ברייתא.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 worked out which רבי שמעון שמואל meant. Here a version of שמואל's statement already includes the words 'of the ברייתא,' so nothing has to be worked out. This confirms the answer and closes the topic.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל rules like רבי שמעון of the ברייתא. One may let blood from a בכור even if it causes a blemish, and may slaughter it because of that blemish.

phrases.english: And Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi
teaches it explicitly:
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha is like Rabbi Shimon of the baraita.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי מַתְנֵי לַהּ בְּהֶדְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the answer of step 11 with a version of שמואל's statement that says it openly.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that שמואל meant רבי שמעון of the ברייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי's version of רב יהודה quoting שמואל, which openly says 'of the ברייתא.'

steps.title: משנה: Slitting the ear of a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: New משנה: someone who slits a בכור's ear may never slaughter it, says רבי אליעזר. The חכמים say that if another blemish appears, he may slaughter it on that one.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone slits the ear of a בכור, he may never slaughter it. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. The חכמים say: if another blemish appears on it, he may slaughter it because of that blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It discusses a person who on purpose makes a blemish in a בכור by slitting its ear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור may be slaughtered and eaten outside the מקדש only if it has a blemish. Here the person made the blemish himself, so he is penalized and may not slaughter it because of that blemish. רבי אליעזר says the penalty lasts forever. The חכמים say a new blemish that appears on its own does permit slaughter.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn male animal, holy to the כהן
Blemish (allows a בכור to be slaughtered)
He may slaughter it because of that blemish

steps.confusionAlert: Even according to the חכמים, the ear-slit itself does not permit slaughter. Only a second blemish that comes on its own does.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who slits the ear of a firstborn,
this one may never slaughter it,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם אַחֵר — יִשְׁחוֹט עָלָיו.
phrases.english: If another blemish develops in it, he may slaughter it on account of that.
phrases.notes: 'That' means the new blemish, not the ear-slit he made himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the blood-letting discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: someone who made a blemish in a בכור may never slaughter it. חכמים: a second blemish that appears on its own permits slaughter.

steps.title: Does רבי אליעזר penalize forever?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי אליעזר really makes a penalty last forever, and begins quoting a contradicting משנה about a person with a בהרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Does רבי אליעזר really penalize forever? Here is a contradiction: one who had a בהרת...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's view in the משנה. It starts quoting another משנה that seems to contradict it, and the quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי אליעזר gives a penalty that never ends. The גמרא sets up a contradiction from a משנה in נגעים about a בהרת, which will suggest that רבי אליעזר does not penalize forever. Here we only see the opening words of that source.

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction
A bright white צרעת mark on the skin

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ וּמִי קָנֵיס רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְעוֹלָם?
phrases.english: GEMARA: But does Rabbi Eliezer penalize forever?
And they raised a contradiction:
One who had a baheret

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי קָנֵיס רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְעוֹלָם? וּרְמִינְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אליעזר's ruling in the משנה of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling that a person who blemished a בכור may never slaughter it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה (about a בהרת) seems to show that רבי אליעזר does not make penalties last forever, so the two rulings conflict.
